part.name: Dual-fan radiator / heat-exchanger module (assembly-like STEP)
part.description: Rectangular heat-exchanger core with peripheral frame/end-tank structure and a dual axial-fan pack (fan rings/guards, hubs, and many small blade/grille faces). STEP is marked invalid and contains many solids/faces typical of an assembly or heavily faceted/segmented model.
part.symmetry_note: Fan pack is approximately symmetric about the mid-plane between the two fan centers; coolant porting/fittings appear asymmetric.

Section.name: Radiator core + perimeter frame
features included: Rectangular core envelope / heat-transfer face fields
Section.function intent: Provide the primary heat-exchange area and a stiff perimeter structure that supports end-tanks and the fan/shroud attachment.
Section.physical behavior: Core faces present large area for convective heat transfer; perimeter frame carries bending and torsion loads from mounts and fan-induced vibration, distributing them around the rectangular boundary to reduce local deformation.
Section.geometry: Large rectangular plate-like envelope with distinct outer planes (top/bottom/front/back/side) plus large BSPLINE face regions representing fin/mesh fields.
Section.location: Central body; spans the full rectangular outline seen in left/right views behind the fan pack.

Section.name: End-tank / manifold region (port corner set A)
features included: Large circular port interface (hose neck seat)
Section.function intent: Collect/distribute coolant from the core into a hose/pipe connection and provide a robust interface for clamped hoses or mating plumbing.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a pressure boundary; cylindrical neck and bead resist hoop stress from internal pressure and clamp loads; blended transitions reduce stress concentration at the tank-to-neck junction.
Section.geometry: Corner region with large cylinder (port bore/OD) and torus-like bead/transition surfaces plus adjacent planar tank boundary faces.
Section.location: One outer corner of the rectangular assembly (corner hose neck visible in iso/right views).

Section.name: End-tank / manifold region (port corner set B)

Section.physical behavior: Similar pressure-boundary behavior to SEC-02; blended transitions spread clamp and pressure loads back into the tank wall and frame.
Section.geometry: Corner region with large cylinder (radius 25.4) and adjacent torus blends/planes mirrored across the part depth.
Section.location: Opposite corner region across the part depth (paired large port).

Section.name: Dual-fan shroud / mounting plate (fan openings + main panel)
Section.function intent: Locate, support, and guard the two axial fans; enforce airflow path through the core by preventing bypass flow around fan perimeters.
Section.physical behavior: Panel behaves as a stiff diaphragm; circular apertures with cylindrical walls resist local buckling and provide accurate fan concentricity; transmits fan torque/vibration to the main frame.
Section.geometry: Large planar shroud face(s) with two large cylindrical cutouts (fan rings) and local edge transitions.
Section.location: On the fan side of the core (right view shows both fans mounted to this plane).

Section.name: Fan assembly A (hub + ring + blades/guard detail set A)
Section.function intent: Generate forced airflow through the core on one side of the module.
Section.physical behavior: Rotating blades create pressure rise and flow; hub/ring geometry constrains the rotating group and provides stiffness; guard/ring reduces finger access and stabilizes flow; detailed small faces represent blade curvature and guard ribs.
Section.geometry: Coaxial cylindrical hub surfaces with toroidal blend bands and many BSPLINE patches representing blade surfaces and guard rib curvature.
Section.location: One of the two circular fans (left fan in the right-view image).

Section.name: Fan assembly B (hub + ring + blades/guard detail set B)
Section.function intent: Generate forced airflow through the core on the second fan position to increase total flow and improve cooling across the rectangular core area.
Section.physical behavior: Mirrors fan A behavior; its rotation/airload is carried into the shroud ring and into the perimeter frame; local ribs/guard distribute contact/vibration loads.
Section.geometry: Second fan’s hub/ring with similar cylindrical and toroidal elements and many BSPLINE blade surfaces.
Section.location: Second fan (right fan in the right-view image).

Section.name: Mounting tabs / corner bosses
Section.function intent: Provide discrete attachment points to the vehicle/chassis (or test fixture), locating the radiator module and carrying static and dynamic loads.
Section.physical behavior: Tabs/bosses work in bearing and shear around fasteners; corner pads reduce local stresses by spreading clamp load into the frame; stiffened corner geometry reduces vibration amplification.
Section.geometry: Small protruding boss/tab solids with relatively simple outer surfaces compared with the core/fan geometry; includes special single-face solids in STEP that likely represent simplified pads.
Section.location: At the outer corners/edges of the rectangular frame (visible as corner features in right/iso views).

Section.name: Auxiliary fittings / small ports (barbs, drains, small bosses)
features included: Small radiused transitions and local bosses
Section.function intent: Provide secondary fluid interfaces (e.g., bleed/drain/aux lines) and/or tooling/fixture features; also includes small clearance/locating bosses.
Section.physical behavior: Small ports see localized clamp/contact loads and internal pressure; blends/chamfers reduce stress at the boss root; small features are prone to fatigue if unsupported so they rely on the tank/frame stiffness nearby.
Section.geometry: Multiple small-radius cylinders and local planar patches; STEP shows many repeated small-cylinder/plane/bspline groups (likely ribs/guard spokes/fastener details).
Section.location: Near lower/side regions where small brass-colored barbs are visible in the views; also scattered around fan/shroud for fasteners and guard ribs.
